newsitem.title: USA: TCF sees Winthrop deal slightly dilutive.
newsitem.headline: TCF sees Winthrop deal slightly dilutive.

text.p: TCF Financial Corp said Friday its proposed $326 million acquisition of Winthrop Resources Corp is likely to be slightly dilutive to earnings per share in the first full year after completion, before becoming accretive after that.

"It probably will dilute, particulalry coming off the blocks, a couple of percentages, first full year of operations and it should be accretive after that," William Cooper, TCF chief executive officer said in a conference call with analysts Friday.

As part of the proposed deal, TCF will issue about 6.9 million shares to shareholders of Wintrhop, a company that leases systems technology equipment to business. Both Winthrop and TCF, a $7.1 billion-asset savings bank holding company, are headquarter in Minneapolis.

Cooper said TCF chose to account for the deal under a pooling of interests method, because a purchase accounting method would have generated a great amount of goodwill, which would have to be written off for several years.
Because the deal will be accounted for under pooling of interests accounting, TCF will have to suspend its share repurchase program for about six months, Cooper said.
Cooper also said the companies will likely have to file for U.S. anti-trust review for the deal, but that he did not expect any anti-trust issues to prevent the deal.
Winthrop shares closed up 3/8 at 34-3/8 Friday and TCF was down 5/8 at 46-1/2.
